data.title: Middle East Eye: ‘They want to displace us’: Israel launches new demolition of West Bank olive groves
data.author: Mohammed Turkman
data.summary:
‘They want to displace us’: Israel launches new demolition of West Bank olive groves
Submitted by
Mohammed Turkman
on
Thu, 10/01/2026 - 12:21
Military orders and bulldozers target Palestinian farmland, threatening livelihoods ahead of the olive harvest
A Palestinian walks among olive trees uprooted by Israeli forces on his land in Beit Rima, northwest of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank (Mohammed Turkman/MEE)
Off
Standing in his backyard, Saleh Tamimi looked in agony at the remains of olive trees he had tended for years.
Around his home in Deir Nizam, northwest of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, the uprooted trees lay in a tangled heap of branches, stones and soil.
Days earlier, Israeli bulldozers had arrived to raze land his family has owned since the 1960s.
“What has this lemon tree done to them and their security?” Tamimi asked Middle East Eye, pointing to the broken branches.
“I used to water this olive tree every day,” he added, pointing to another.
He said his house has also been issued a demolition order.
“They want to displace us. I have nowhere else to go. Even if they destroy this house, I’m not leaving.”
Tamimi’s case is part of a wider campaign targeting Palestinian agricultural land and olive groves across the occupied West Bank.
In September, a series of military orders demanded the removal of vegetation and uprooting of trees across hundreds of dunams, just weeks before the olive harvest began.
According to data from the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission, 55 military orders targeting trees and vegetation were issued between the start of the year and September.
They affected about 2,373 dunams, compared with 47 orders covering 1,613 dunams throughout the whole of 2025.
On 20 September, following the killing of a settler in a shooting near Deir Nizam, the commission said a military order was issued targeting about 99.79 dunams of village land. The order required vegetation to be removed and olive and other trees to be uprooted.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'
UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a "terrorist act" and used the cockpit's emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.
Initial findings from the UAE's investigation into the attack also did not confirm his nationality, according to a report on Saturday from the country's state news agency WAM, but a Saudi source has confirmed to AFP that he was Omani.
Media reports have also said he had been barred from flying in his home nation over concerns about extremist views.
The reports came as the first flight carrying Israelis home from the United Arab Emirates landed in Tel Aviv after services were suspended following the attack, according to Israel's airport authority website.
"The co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act" and had "attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft," WAM quoted UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying, referring to initial findings of an investigation.
Reporting by AFP

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'The entire land is ours': Ben Gvir escalates calls for annexation of occupied West Bank
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
'The entire land is ours': Ben Gvir escalates calls for annexation of occupied West Bank
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir claimed that the entire occupied West Bank “belongs to Israel” and has vowed to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and pursue the displacement of Palestinians if he becomes defence minister, Israeli media have reported.
Speaking to Israel’s Channel 14, Ben Gvir said that, if appointed defence minister, he would work to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and push for Palestinians to leave the occupied West Bank and Gaza.
The minister said that 60 percent of Palestinians want to “emigrate”.
“I will dedicate time to this, and I will manage the process continuously. Every week, I will hold a discussion involving all relevant parties,” he said. “There is no difference between Areas A, B and C. The entire land is ours."
Under the territorial framework established in the Oslo agreement between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1995, Areas A and B were placed under varying degrees of Palestinian jurisdiction, while Israel retained control over Area C.

Gaza death toll rises after seven Palestinians killed in 24 hours
Gaza's death toll has reached 74,229 after seven more Palestinians were killed by Israel in the last 24 hours, the enclave's health ministry reports.
The ministry said that seven Palestinians have been killed and 20 others wounded in Israeli attacks in the last 24 hours. The figure includes two people who succumbed to injuries from previous attacks and one whose body was retrieved from rubble.
According to the ministry, some 1,445 Palestinians have been killed, 5,052 wounded and 835 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble since the so-called "ceasefire" came into effect in October 2024.
On Thursday, thousands gathered for a mass funeral for over 100 bodies belonging to victims trapped beneath the debris of a residential tower, which was flattened by Israeli strikes at the beginning of the genocide in October 2023.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Why the EU's sanctions on Sudan's gold trade are fundamentally flawed
data.author: Osama Abuzaid
data.summary:
Why the EU's sanctions on Sudan's gold trade are fundamentally flawed
Submitted by
Osama Abuzaid
on
Wed, 09/23/2026 - 08:41
Sanctioning bullion, while leaving much of the infrastructure facilitating its movement intact, risks treating the symptoms of Sudan's war economy rather than its architecture
A group of armed defectors from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) arrive in Omdurman, Sudan, 19 August 2026 (Ebrahim Hamid/AFP)
Off
For more than three years, Sudan has been trapped in a war that has shattered cities, emptied villages and pushed millions into displacement. Since fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in 2023, international diplomacy produced no shortage of conferences, ceasefire proposals and mediation initiatives.
Yet each new round of negotiations has been overtaken by renewed violence on the ground. The human cost has continued to rise, with more than 150,000 people estimated dead, over 14 million displaced, and famine spreading across parts of Sudan.
Against this backdrop, the EU has increasingly turned to sanctions as its principal instrument of engagement. Its latest package, adopted in July 2026, represents a notable shift. Rather than expanding the practice of blacklisting individuals and companies, Brussels moved to target Sudan's war economy, banning imports of Sudanese gold and prohibiting exports of mercury and cyanide used in gold extraction.
The change is significant, but raises a larger question. Can economic sanctions succeed when they target the commodity that finances the war while leaving intact the regional networks making that trade profitable?
The EU is not new to sanctions against Sudan. It has maintained an arms embargo since the mid-1990s, later incorporating its measures into the UN sanctions regime on Darfur. data.summary:
Yemeni army claims 1,540 Houthi casualties as fighting intensifies in Taiz
The Yemeni government has claimed that 1,540 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded during the past 24 hours as the battles raging in the southwestern governorate of Taiz intensified.
The Yemeni army said it carried out 474 operations against Houthi positions, reinforcements, command centres and military capabilities across several fronts, with most of the reported casualties concentrated in Taiz.
Military spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said that the raids included warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and rocket launchers.
The latest claims come as Taiz heats up as one of the main battlegrounds in Yemen's renewed conflict.
Government forces have reported repeated clashes across the province in recent weeks, including around Bani Bakari, Maqbanah, al-Aqroud and the northern and eastern approaches to Taiz city.

data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Eight Palestinians, including mother and daughter, killed in attacks across Gaza since dawn
Eight Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza since dawn, Al Jazeera reports, citing medical sources.
Five people were killed in an Israeli attack on a residential block in Gaza City, including one in Beit Lahia, while two others succumbed to wounds sustained in previous attacks.
Wafa news agency reported earlier that Muhammad Talaat Aqel succumbed to a gunshot wound to his head, which he had sustained in an attack days before.
Reuters reports that four women were among the five killed in the apartment block attack. Medics and the local church reported that Maisa Abu Dawoud, and her daughter Mary, were among the victims. The attack reportedly levelled the building, causing a fire to rip through the debris.
"We were asleep and suddenly heard continuous strikes and heavy explosions. The children woke up startled and started running and screaming," witness Ahmed Al-Dahdouh told Reuters.
"We ran out and found that our neighbour's house was struck and there were dismembered martyrs, women, men and children. We started to pull them out. They were scattered under the rubble," he said.
